name: Ownership Standards
info:
Architectural Principle

Each responsibility has exactly one authoritative owner.

Application Services

- Every external device or external system is represented by an Application Service.
- An Application Service owns the runtime state and business logic for its device or system.

Infrastructure Services

- Shared responsibilities shall be implemented as Infrastructure Services.
- Infrastructure Services own the runtime state and business logic associated with the shared responsibility.
- Infrastructure Services do not own the runtime state of Application Services.

Rules

- Every piece of runtime information has exactly one authoritative owner.
- Services shall not directly modify another Service's runtime state.
- Services communicate through events and shared infrastructure.

name: Event Standards
info:
Event Standards
===============

Architectural Principle

Services communicate by publishing and consuming events.

Definition

An event is an immutable statement of fact published by a Service that
describes an observation or a state change that has already occurred.

An event reports what happened.

An event does not:
    - Request action.
    - Direct another Service.
    - Infer the cause of an observation.

Rules

- Events describe observations or completed state changes.
- Events shall not contain inferred conclusions.
- Events shall report only facts known to the publishing Service.
- Events shall contain only the information required by consumers.
- Services publish events without knowledge of which Services consume them.

Event Naming

- Event types shall be UPPER_CASE.
- Event types shall describe what occurred.
- Event names shall be nouns describing observations or completed state changes, not requested actions.

Examples

    HEARTBEAT_RECEIVED
    HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT
    ALERT_CREATED
    ALERT_RESOLVED
    DEVICE_REGISTERED
    GPS_POSITION_UPDATED

Guidelines

Use:

    ALERT_CREATED

Avoid:

    SEND_EMAIL

Use:

    HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT

Avoid:

    DEVICE_FAILED

The preferred form reports an observable fact.
The avoided form requests an action or reports a conclusion.

Event Ownership

- The publishing Service is the authoritative owner of the event.
- Once published, the meaning of an event shall not be changed.
- Consumers act upon events but shall not reinterpret or alter their meaning.

name: Services
info:
Services
========

Architectural Principle

Every Service shall follow a common structure and lifecycle. Consistent
organization improves readability, maintainability, and simplifies the
addition of new Services.

Service Layout

Every Service shall have the following layout:

    Service Information      (Comment)
    Initialization           (Function)
    Event Handler            (Function)
    Library Functions        (Comment)
    Utilities                (Optional)
    Diagnostics              (Optional)

Service Initialization

Every Service shall include an Initialization function using the
following header:

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Initialize <Service Name>
//
// Executed once during Node-RED startup.
//
// Creates the <Service Name> runtime object. Runtime relationships with other
// Services are established later through registration.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Initialization Rules

- Initialization executes exactly once during Node-RED startup.
- Initialization creates only the Service's runtime object.
- Initialization shall not establish relationships with other Services.
- Initialization shall not register devices or Services.
- Runtime relationships are established later through registration.
- Event processing begins only after initialization and registration have
  completed.

<script>
    (function () {

    let savedDistanceFromBottom = 0;
    let savedScrollHeight = 0;

    const FOLLOW_THRESHOLD = 30;

    function getDistanceFromBottom(wrapper) {
        return (
            wrapper.scrollHeight -
            wrapper.scrollTop -
            wrapper.clientHeight
        );
    }

    function scrollToBottom(wrapper) {
        wrapper.scrollTop = wrapper.scrollHeight;
    }

    function savePosition(wrapper) {
        savedDistanceFromBottom =
            getDistanceFromBottom(wrapper);

        savedScrollHeight =
            wrapper.scrollHeight;
    }

    function restorePosition(wrapper) {
        const newScrollHeight = wrapper.scrollHeight;

        const logGrowth =
            newScrollHeight - savedScrollHeight;

        if (savedDistanceFromBottom <= FOLLOW_THRESHOLD) {
            scrollToBottom(wrapper);
            return;
        }

        const targetDistanceFromBottom =
            savedDistanceFromBottom + logGrowth;

        wrapper.scrollTop =
            newScrollHeight -
            wrapper.clientHeight -
            targetDistanceFromBottom;
    }

    function start(wrapper) {

        wrapper.addEventListener("scroll", function () {
            savePosition(wrapper);
        });

        const observer = new MutationObserver(function () {
            restorePosition(wrapper);
        });

        observer.observe(wrapper, {
            childList: true,
            subtree: true
        });

        scrollToBottom(wrapper);

        savedDistanceFromBottom = 0;
        savedScrollHeight = wrapper.scrollHeight;
    }

    function findWrapper() {

        const wrapper = document.querySelector(
            "#nrdb-ui-widget-6008f8352f3b3176 .tabulator-tableholder"
        );

        if (!wrapper) {
            setTimeout(findWrapper, 250);
            return;
        }

        start(wrapper);
    }

    findWrapper();

})();
</script>

<script>
(function () {

    let savedDistanceFromBottom = 0;
    let savedScrollHeight = 0;

    const FOLLOW_THRESHOLD = 30;


    function getDistanceFromBottom(wrapper) {

        return (
            wrapper.scrollHeight -
            wrapper.scrollTop -
            wrapper.clientHeight
        );
    }


    function scrollToBottom(wrapper) {

        wrapper.scrollTop = wrapper.scrollHeight;
    }


    function savePosition(wrapper) {

        savedDistanceFromBottom =
            getDistanceFromBottom(wrapper);

        savedScrollHeight =
            wrapper.scrollHeight;

        console.log(
            "LOG SCROLL:",
            "distanceFromBottom =",
            savedDistanceFromBottom,
            "scrollHeight =",
            savedScrollHeight
        );
    }


    function restorePosition(wrapper) {

        const newScrollHeight = wrapper.scrollHeight;

        const logGrowth =
            newScrollHeight - savedScrollHeight;


        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // User was at or very near the bottom.
        // Follow the new bottom.
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------

        if (savedDistanceFromBottom <= FOLLOW_THRESHOLD) {

            scrollToBottom(wrapper);

            console.log(
                "LOG UPDATE: following bottom"
            );

            return;
        }


        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // User was reading older events.
        //
        // Preserve the same content in the viewport by compensating for
        // everything added to the log since the position was saved.
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------

        const targetDistanceFromBottom =
            savedDistanceFromBottom + logGrowth;


        wrapper.scrollTop =
            newScrollHeight -
            wrapper.clientHeight -
            targetDistanceFromBottom;


        console.log(
            "LOG UPDATE: restored position",
            "previousDistanceFromBottom =",
            savedDistanceFromBottom,
            "logGrowth =",
            logGrowth,
            "targetDistanceFromBottom =",
            targetDistanceFromBottom
        );
    }


    function start(wrapper) {

        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Save the user's actual position whenever they scroll.
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------

        wrapper.addEventListener("scroll", function () {

            savePosition(wrapper);

        });


        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Dashboard 2 may reposition the table when its data changes.
        // Once that happens, compensate for the amount the log grew.
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------

        const observer = new MutationObserver(function () {

            restorePosition(wrapper);

        });


        observer.observe(wrapper, {
            childList: true,
            subtree: true
        });


        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Initial display starts at the newest events.
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------

        scrollToBottom(wrapper);

        savedDistanceFromBottom = 0;
        savedScrollHeight = wrapper.scrollHeight;
    }


    function findWrapper() {

        const wrapper = document.querySelector(
            '.nrdb-ui-table .v-table__wrapper'
        );

        if (!wrapper) {
            setTimeout(findWrapper, 250);
            return;
        }

        start(wrapper);
    }


    findWrapper();

})();
</script>

name: Alert Management Rules
info:
Alert Management Rules
Rule 1 — Device/Service Owns Condition Detection
A device/service is the authoritative owner of the conditions it monitors.
Examples:
Heartbeat owns device online/offline.
GPS owns GPS fix quality.
RO owns fresh water level.
Network owns Wi-Fi connectivity.
Notification never determines whether a condition exists.
Rule 2 — Device/Service Owns Active Alert State
Each device/service maintains a table of its currently active alerts.
An active alert exists only while the monitored condition exists.
The device/service uses g_findAlert() to determine whether a condition has already been reported.
Rule 3 — Create Alert
When a condition first occurs:
Create an ACTIVE_NOTIF.
Initialize:
startedAt
lastReceivedAt
lastNotification
nextNotification
notificationCount
Pass the alert to Notification.
Rule 4 — Update Alert
While the condition continues to exist, the device/service updates the active alert as required.
Typical updates include:
lastReceivedAt
lastNotification
nextNotification
notificationCount
The device/service determines when an update is necessary.
Rule 5 — Resolve Alert
When the condition no longer exists:
Locate the active alert using g_findAlert().
Set:
resolvedAt = Date.now()
Pass the resolved alert to Notification.
If no active alert exists, no action is required.
Rule 6 — Notification Owns Delivery
Notification receives alerts from device/services.
Notification is responsible for:
Looking up ALERT_CONFIG.
Sending email.
Writing log entries.
Updating dashboards.
Any future delivery mechanisms.
Device/services never send notifications directly.
Rule 7 — Notification Owns Completion
After successfully processing a resolved alert:
Remove the alert from the originating device/service's active alert table.
Notification is responsible for final cleanup of the alert lifecycle.
Responsibilities Summary
Device/Service	Notification
Detect conditions	Deliver notifications
Create alerts	Email
Update alerts	Logging
Resolve alerts	Dashboard updates
Maintain active alert table	Apply ALERT_CONFIG
Remove completed alerts

Heartbeat Service
info:
Heartbeat Service

Purpose
-------
The Heartbeat Service monitors communication with registered devices and
services. It detects when communication has been lost or restored and
manages heartbeat-related alerts.

Responsibilities
----------------
- Monitor heartbeat activity for registered devices and services.
- Record the time of the last successful check-in.
- Determine when communication has been lost.
- Determine when communication has been restored.
- Create ACTIVE_ALERT records when communication is lost.
- Resolve ACTIVE_ALERT records when communication is restored.
- Maintain heartbeat runtime state.

Owns
----
- Heartbeat runtime state.
- Last successful check-in times.
- Online/offline status.
- Missed heartbeat statistics.
- Active heartbeat alerts.

Does Not
--------
- Send email notifications.
- Display dashboard notifications.
- Determine notification policy.
- Delete resolved alerts.
- Diagnose the cause of communication failures.

Observations
------------
The Heartbeat Service reports only observable facts.

Examples:
- Communication with a device has been lost.
- Communication with a device has been restored.
- The last successful check-in occurred at a specific time.

The Heartbeat Service does not infer why communication was lost.

Collaborates With
-----------------
Notification Service
    - Receives newly created alerts.
    - Receives resolved alerts.

Configuration
    - Provides heartbeat timing and timeout configuration.

Device Services
    - Produce heartbeat messages.
    - May query heartbeat status.

Public Interface
----------------
Initially anticipated:
- Process heartbeat received.
- Check heartbeat timeouts.
- Create heartbeat alert.
- Resolve heartbeat alert.

info:
Owning Service
      │
      ▼
Create ALERT_CONFIG
      │
      ▼
Alert Management Service
      │
      ▼
Policy Exists?
 ┌────┴────┐
 │         │
Yes        No
 │         │
 ▼         ▼
Done    Register Policy
             │
             ▼
      Persist Policy

Every alert is logged.
An originating service reports an alert only when its state changes.
Alert Management maintains the collection of active alerts.
An alert can remain active indefinitely without the originating service sending anything else.
Initial email is delayed according to the alert's policy.
Email reminders occur at the top of the hour, not one hour after the previous email.
All currently active alerts are aggregated into the notification.
Resolving an alert removes it from the active collection and cancels its pending notification activity.
The resolution itself is logged.
Email behavior associated with resolution is part of the close-out policy.
